sections.h2: Selling a house in Horn Lake
sections.html:
Horn Lake sits on the Tennessee line, directly south of Memphis, in DeSoto County. U.S. 51 follows much of the eastern boundary and leads 15 miles north into downtown Memphis and 9 miles south to Hernando, where the county seat is. Interstate 55 clips the east side with Exits 287, 289 and 901. Southaven lies east and southeast of town, and Goodman Road, which doubles as Mississippi Highways 301 and 302, carries most east-west traffic.

The 2020 census put the city at 26,736 people on about 16.3 square miles. Housing units total 10,987 against 10,072 households, and the median household income is $53,311. Some of the difference between units and households is vacant homes: listings, rentals and houses between occupants. When the empty one is yours, utilities, insurance and upkeep keep landing on you every month.

Memphis pulls on this market, so plenty of Horn Lake owners have a Tennessee employer, lender or relative. Before hiring anyone, confirm that your title company and insurer are active in Mississippi. Your deed, your tax bill and your disclosure form all follow Mississippi law.

Buyers in Horn Lake mostly want to know about the drive. Memphis International Airport is about seven miles from the center of town, downtown Memphis is 15 miles up U.S. 51, and the county seat in Hernando is 9 miles the other way. A street near Goodman Road or the Interstate 55 exits is worth highlighting to any buyer, since commuters count those minutes.

Horn Lake also has plenty of land and not much water: the city covers 16.3 square miles, nearly all of it land. Neighborhoods vary a lot from one side of town to the other, so the number a buyer will pay depends far more on your block and the condition of your house than on any citywide average.

Plan review, permit approval and business licensing sit in the Planning and Development Department, and permit requests are filed through an online portal. Code Enforcement works from 3101 Goodman Road West. Reach it by calling 662-342-3507, writing to codeviolations@hornlake.org, or using the city's 311 request page.

Rental owners should watch a pending rental housing code. As drafted, its purpose is to set a floor for rental housing so that slum and blighted conditions get prevented or repaired. Landlords planning to sell should call the city before closing and find out whether the final version reaches their house.

  • Hunt for permits an earlier owner or contractor never closed.
  • Ask whether anyone has filed a complaint against your address.
  • Settle your final water and sanitation bills, which are paid to the city.

The full ordinances are on Municode. Closing out loose ends early means fewer corrections on the settlement statement.

A Mississippi parcel's tax bill must be settled by February 1, and it covers the assessment year before. DeSoto County lets you pay at a collector's office (Hernando, Olive Branch or Horn Lake), by mail, or through its website. The state sets the ratios: a house its owner lives in counts at 10 percent of true value, while rentals, vacant houses and other real property count at 15 percent.

Homestead exemption is claimed through the county Tax Assessor, with a filing season that runs January 1 to April 1. This time the window opens at 8:00 AM on January 4, 2027 and shuts at 5:00 PM on April 1, 2027. New filers go to 365 Losher Street, Suite 100 in Hernando.

With a spring closing, expect your title company to apportion that year's bill and show you the numbers ahead of signing.

If you disagree with a valuation, take it to the Board of Supervisors by the first Monday in August, which is the normal cutoff. Counties must reassess real property within every four-year span, so a big jump can appear after years of little change. Pull the notice, jot down what you believe the house would sell for and why, and gather photos of any damage or wear that an assessor driving by would miss.

Timing matters if a sale is coming. Whatever the final assessment is, the year's bill gets divided at closing, so a lower number helps you and the buyer alike.

sections.h2: Choosing between a listing, a private sale and cash
sections.html:
Horn Lake owners can pick from three paths. Hiring an agent can fetch the best price for a clean, updated house if you are fine with showings, an inspection and waiting on the buyer's mortgage. Going it alone spares you the commission yet leaves contract and negotiation in your hands. Cash is fastest and takes the house as it stands.

Inherited property, deferred repairs and tenant trouble are the common reasons people choose cash here, since nobody hands you a repair list. Get any offer in writing, ask how the amount was reached, and set it beside the net from a listing after agent fees, fix-up costs and several months of mortgage, tax and utility bills. We promise nothing on price, and saying no costs you nothing.

Pulling documents together early shortens every route. Locate the deed, the newest tax bill, the last few utility statements, receipts for roof, HVAC and plumbing work, and any permit sign-offs. If a tenant lives in the house, add the lease and the rent record. A buyer or title officer who can see these answers in one folder is far less likely to stall over a question.

Under Mississippi Code Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523, a covered seller needs to give the buyer the written property condition disclosure statement ahead of the title transfer. Answer each line honestly. Receipts for past repairs help you respond when a buyer asks about the roof or the plumbing.

  • First, a contract gets signed.
  • A title search reveals liens and unpaid taxes.
  • Your mortgage, back taxes or any city balance get paid from the proceeds.
  • You sign the deed at the closing table, and the DeSoto County Chancery Clerk records it afterward.

Show up with photo identification, a payoff letter if a mortgage is outstanding, and permit or repair records. A cash buyer needs no lender, so appraisal and loan underwriting never enter the picture, and the calendar gets shorter.

For a cloudy title or a question about who has authority to sign, go to an attorney or the title company.

faqs.a: Horn Lake is in DeSoto County in the northwest corner of the state. It borders Southaven and lies roughly 15 miles south of downtown Memphis along U.S. 51.

faqs.q: When can I file for homestead exemption in DeSoto County?
faqs.a: The window opens at 8:00 AM on January 4, 2027 and closes at 5:00 PM on April 1, 2027. A first-time filer goes to the Tax Assessor's Office at 365 Losher Street, Suite 100, Hernando.

faqs.q: Who handles a code complaint in Horn Lake?
faqs.a: Code Enforcement takes them at 662-342-3507 or codeviolations@hornlake.org. The office is at 3101 Goodman Road West.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property taxes if I live in Horn Lake?
faqs.a: The DeSoto County tax collector has offices in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake, and also accepts mail and online payments. The bill is due by February 1.

faqs.q: Must a seller give a written disclosure in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Yes for covered sellers: the written statement is due as soon as practicable ahead of the title transfer (Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523). An attorney can tell you if your sale is exempt.
